prompt:
Research the officially documented limits of the Telegram Bot API: messages per second, file upload and download size. Cite Telegram's own documentation or FAQ and quote the limits.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Here are the officially documented limits for the Telegram Bot API regarding messages per second and file upload/download sizes:

SOURCE: https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq/ | QUOTE: "For bulk notifications, bots are not able to broadcast more than about 30 messages per second" | CLAIM: The limit for bulk broadcast messages per second is approximately 30.
SOURCE: https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq/ | QUOTE: "In a single chat, avoid sending more than one message per second." | CLAIM: The limit for messages per second in a single chat is 1.
SOURCE: https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq/ | QUOTE: "Bots can currently send files of any type of up to 50 MB in size" | CLAIM: The maximum file upload size for bots using the official Bot API is 50 MB.
SOURCE: https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq/ | QUOTE: "Use the getFile method. Please note that this will only work with files of up to 20 MB in size." | CLAIM: The maximum file download size for bots using the official Bot API is 20 MB.
